mission.description: Screen the coastal track northeast of the landing cove and establish an observation post on the low ridge at 2100,1900 overlooking the inland approach.

I then swing wide through 1950,1680 to the ridge, keeping a 200m avoid ring around the infantry at 1700,1650 whose close-range fires would shred a thin-skinned car.

reasoning.tradeoffs: Hugging the folds is slower than the road my scout car takes, but it keeps the vehicle's guns off my team; taking the road instead would be quicker yet would trade my only cover for speed I do not need on foot. Cover wins for dismounts.
reasoning.what_if_rejected: If I leave the enemy section on the ridge, it occupies the exact ground I need for the OP and turns my observation post into their ambush, and the scout car loses the eyes that keep it out of the infantry's grasp.

reasoning.situation_assessment: That same enemy light vehicle at 1250,3150 is the raid's fast flanker and needs pinning from two sides, while the APC at 1300,3300 and MRAP at 1450,3350 both outmatch my thin scout car if I stray south into their reach. My light vehicle at 1820,3010 can pair with the MRAP to trap the enemy runner.

Two scout cars converging beat one, and I stay well clear of the vehicles that would beat me.

reasoning.what_if_rejected: If I do not help trap the enemy light, it slips the MRAP's grasp and races onto the OP, or worse, draws my scout car south into the APC's arc where it is destroyed for nothing.

My rifle team at 1780,3020 is the last line holding the OP itself at 1750,3000.

My dismounts are the anchor the armored fight is protecting, not a maneuver element against vehicles.

reasoning.what_if_rejected: If the infantry leave their positions to engage the vehicles, they are cut down in the open and the OP is left empty, so even a winning armor fight loses the ground it was meant to keep.
